title: The Machine That Ran the Village
subtitle: 科技与创新 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 科技与创新（科学与技术·科技发展与信息技术创新、科学精神）
meta: 主题语境：科技与创新（科学与技术·科技发展与信息技术创新、科学精神）　|　核心词汇：system　|　正文 391 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 system 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1998 our village installed the first computer anyone there had owned. It ran a single ① system: a list of who owed what for the water. Before it there had been a ② system too, which was Mrs Powell's memory and a pencil, and which had worked for thirty-one years without ever being switched off. A system, I have since noticed, is usually admired only after the one it replaces has died.

I was twelve and appointed, by nobody, to operate it. The ③ system itself was simple — three fields, one button — and the difficulty was entirely human: half the village had two names, a quarter had a name the machine could not spell, and one household had been arguing about the bill since 1974. Every ④ system, my father said, is a description of the people who built it, and this one described nobody in particular.

It was ⑤ systematic in the way machines are and not in the way villages are. Mrs Powell's pencil had allowed for a widow in February; the machine allowed for nothing. By the second winter three households had been cut off for non-payment, all three of them by ⑥ system rather than by anybody's decision, and Mrs Powell walked to the council offices with a list and came back with the water reconnected.

The ⑦ system was replaced in 2004 by a better one, and that one in 2011, and each time the description improved and the allowance did not. What the later ⑧ systems did, which the pencil had never done, was record: eleven years of who paid late, who paid early, and who had argued since 1974. Data, the council called it, and the system believed them. Mrs Powell called it remembering things about people who had not agreed to be remembered.

I work with computers now, and I have built three systems myself, none of which allowed for a widow in February, and I have been trying to get that village out of my ⑨ system ever since without much success. ⑩ The system, I have learned, is not the machine: it is the machine plus the person who decides what to do when the machine is wrong. In our village that person was Mrs Powell, and when she died in 2009 the water bills were correct for the first and only time, and three households went without.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 系统；（计算机的）操作系统
B. n. 制度；体制；成套办法
C. n. 体系；网络（供水、交通等）
D. adj. 有条理的；成体系的（systematic）
E. 固定搭配：by system 按制度（而非个人决定）
F. n. 方法；办法；一套做法
G. 固定搭配：get sth out of one's system 把……排遣掉；从（身心里）除去
H. n. 既定秩序；既成流程（the system）

items.q: Before it there had been a system too
Every system, my father said, is a description
It was systematic in the way machines are
all three of them by system rather than by anybody's decision
get that village out of my system ever since
The system, I have learned, is not the machine

answers.why: 指机器上运行的那一个“系统”，即水费账目程序。
指此前的“一套做法、办法”：Mrs Powell 的记性和一支铅笔。
指系统本身很简单：三个字段、一个按钮。
此处 system 抽象为“制度、体制”，说它是对建造者的描述。
systematic 作形容词，意为“有条理的、成体系的”，与村庄的方式相对。
by system 意为“按制度、按流程”，不是任何人的决定。
指整套供水管理与计费“体系”，2004 年被更好的替换。
指后来的几代“系统”，说它们真正做的是记录。
get sth out of one's system 意为“把……排遣掉、从身心除去”，此处说作者始终忘不了那个村子。
the system 指“既定秩序、整套流程”，说它不等于机器本身。
